questions.answer: Nebulised lidocaine or a transtracheal injection

questions.stem: Why must blood, secretions or vomit be cleared from the airway before topicalisation?
questions.answer: Otherwise the drug cannot reach the mucosa

questions.answer: Limited systemic uptake from the upper airway

questions.stem: Why is a vasoconstrictor needed when topicalising the nose?
questions.answer: To reduce bleeding and shrink the mucosa, making room for the scope and tube

questions.stem: When is ultrasound guidance most useful for airway topicalisation nerve blocks?
options: When landmarks are easy to feel, as in slim patients
When the procedure is very short
When landmarks are hard to feel, e.g. obesity
When the block is needed without any local anaesthetic
